verified.entry_point: library API: new XMLParser(options).parse(xml); caller-registered values enter through parser.addEntity(key, value). Every security and functional case drives the package's canonical ESM entry (self-reference 'fast-xml-parser' -> src/fxp.js).
sites: src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:439-458 (replaceEntitiesValue: DOCTYPE, predefined and HTML/numeric replacement loops; no bound at the pinned commit)
src/xmlparser/OptionsBuilder.js:30-46 (processEntities is a boolean; no limits and no normalisation at the pinned commit)
src/xmlparser/DocTypeReader.js:112-116 (entity values are read with no size or count bound)
src/xmlparser/XMLParser.js:46-56 and src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:76-86 (caller-registered values enter the same expansion path)
routes: T1: a DOCTYPE-declared entity (no '&' in its value) referenced many times in element text or an attribute
T5: a declared value containing no '&' but containing a replacement pattern, so String.replace duplicates surrounding text
T2: the same document-driven substitution through the predefined and HTML/numeric tables, which the first published fix did not count
T3: a large value registered by the caller, referenced a few times from a small document; the count bound alone does not bound the output
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own top-level Jasmine suite (289 specs, 1 pending, 0 failures) from a pristine copy of the pinned spec tree, on the pinned code, the reference and every check patch.

traps.shape: A DOCTYPE declares one ordinary entity whose value has no '&', then the element text or an attribute references it many times. The parser replaces every reference with no bound on the replacement count or on the total growth of the output.
security_tests: entity processing resource bounds bounds a declared entity referenced many times in element text
entity processing resource bounds bounds a declared entity referenced many times in an attribute
coupled_functional_tests: entity processing keeps working keeps chained substitution inside a document
entity processing keeps working allows a legitimate document that stays inside the bounds
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-jmr7-xgp7-cmfj) at the pinned commit; the same loop is used for text and attributes

traps.shape: A declared value with no '&' is passed as the replacement string of String.replace. A value such as "$'" duplicates the text around every reference, so a document that looks inert grows without bound. A count-only bound passes it; making the replacement literal or bounding total growth closes it, while a rule that refuses '$' values breaks legitimate ones.
security_tests: entity processing resource bounds bounds growth caused by a declared replacement value
coupled_functional_tests: entity processing keeps working allows a legitimate document that stays inside the bounds
entity processing keeps working keeps chained substitution inside a document
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit: the declared value is the second argument of String.replace, whose '$' forms are special

traps.shape: The same document-driven substitution runs in the predefined-entity and HTML/numeric tables. A budget added only around the DOCTYPE loop leaves those tables uncounted, so a document can exceed the configured reference limit through them.
security_tests: entity processing resource bounds applies the configured reference limit to numeric character references
entity processing resource bounds applies the configured reference limit to the predefined entities
coupled_functional_tests: entity processing keeps working decodes numeric character references and leaves out-of-range ones alone
entity processing keeps working keeps ordinary references and the disable switch unchanged
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the second published fix (bd26122) added counting to exactly these loops after the first fix left them open

traps.shape: A value registered by the caller is stored in the same standard-entity table. References to it are counted but its expanded length is not, so a tiny document that references a large registered value produces output far beyond the configured growth bound. The output bound must cover that table, or the value must be size-checked when it is registered.
security_tests: entity processing resource bounds bounds references to a value made available by the caller
coupled_functional_tests: entity processing keeps working expands a small value registered by the caller and lets it override a built-in
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the lastEntities loop tracks replacement count only, and none of the published fixes applies the growth bound there
